body.statement: For every \(\vartheta\in\mathcal F_B(p)\) in the no-selection overlap satisfying \(\mathcal K_{\mathrm K}(P_{\vartheta})\), the simultaneous equations in the proof of Kawakami (2021), Theorem 1 on pages 12135--12137 identify \(\omega_0^{\mathrm K}\) and \(\omega_1^{\mathrm K}\). If \(\mathcal T_B(p)\) is a singleton, its atlas value agrees with \(\tau(\vartheta)=\phi_{\mathrm K}(\omega_0^{\mathrm K},\omega_1^{\mathrm K})\). Kawakami's identified scope is the four joint probabilities of binary potential-outcome types, together with their treatment-conditional weights used for PN and PS, under Figure 2(b), equation (2), and Theorem 1(i)--(iii). For the single explicit selected boundary datum \((p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})\), \(\mathcal F_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal T_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})=\{(1/2,1/2)\}\), but \(A_x^{\mathrm K}(b^{\mathrm{bd}})\) is singular for each \(x\): because \(\mathcal W=\{w_1,w_2,w_3\}\), its first column is the sum of its last three columns. Thus this legal selected response-cycle law violates the named invertibility assumption in Kawakami's Theorem 1(i) while remaining classified by the atlas; this is a strict scope separation, not a subsumption claim.
body.justification: The result derives exact target agreement on Kawakami's regular overlap and proves one selected singular law lies outside its loading-matrix domain.
body.gap: Kawakami's regular IV-plus-proxy theorem does not classify selected nonnegative response-cycle faces.
body.consumer: IV-plus-proxy users can distinguish overlap agreement from strict scope separation without a subsumption claim.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(\vartheta\in\mathcal F_B(p)\) satisfy the stated no-selection overlap and \(\mathcal K_{\mathrm K}(P_\vartheta)\).  The cited Kawakami identification lemma applies under exactly the recursive factorization, invertibility, separation, and exclusion conditions included in \(\mathcal K_{\mathrm K}\); its simultaneous equations identify \(\omega_0^{\mathrm K}\) and \(\omega_1^{\mathrm K}\).

In the comparator order \((00,01,10,11)\), response consistency implies that \(X=1,Y=1\) admits precisely types \(01\) and \(11\), while \(X=0,Y=0\) admits precisely types \(00\) and \(01\).  Selected-table positivity and \(S=1\) almost surely make both conditioning events positive.  Therefore
\[
\operatorname{PN}(\vartheta)
=\frac{\omega^{\mathrm K}_{1,2}}
{\omega^{\mathrm K}_{1,2}+\omega^{\mathrm K}_{1,4}},
\qquad
\operatorname{PS}(\vartheta)
=\frac{\omega^{\mathrm K}_{0,2}}
{\omega^{\mathrm K}_{0,1}+\omega^{\mathrm K}_{0,2}}, \tag{16}
\]
which is \(\tau(\vartheta)=\phi_{\mathrm K}(\omega_0^{\mathrm K},\omega_1^{\mathrm K})\).  If \(\mathcal T_B(p)\) is a singleton, it contains \(\tau(\vartheta)\) by definition; hence (16) is its unique value.  The full-rigidity theorem makes the atlas value equal to that unique element.  The cited Kawakami lemma also supplies the stated identified scope: four joint binary potential-outcome-type probabilities and the treatment-conditional weights recovered in its proof.

It remains to verify the strict scope-separation datum.  By the already established experimental-proxy reduction and boundary-separation theorem,
\[
\mathcal F_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})\ne\varnothing,
\qquad
\mathcal T_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})=\{(1/2,1/2)\}. \tag{17}
\]
For either \(x\), each row of \(A_x^{\mathrm K}(b^{\mathrm{bd}})\) is
\[
(1,b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}(w_1),b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}(w_2),b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}(w_3)).
\]
Because \(b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}\) is a probability vector on the three-point alphabet,
\[
1=b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}(w_1)+b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}(w_2)+b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}(w_3)
\]
row by row.  Hence the first column of \(A_x^{\mathrm K}(b^{\mathrm{bd}})\) is the sum of its last three columns, so its determinant is zero for \(x=0,1\).  The datum therefore violates the named invertibility condition in Kawakami's Theorem 1(i), while (17) and the full atlas give a legal selected rigid law.  This establishes a one-law strict scope separation and makes no subsumption claim.
